thread:
Samir Gupta: heads-up: saw duplicate webhook deliveries again. this time its hedged clients + gateway local retry + transient backpressure during fastpath demotion. thinking we need a small contract to tie hedges + gateway retries together so downstreams can deterministically dedupe.
Omar Khan: send the short trace? curious where two deliveries diverged.
Samir Gupta: minimal trace:
```
CLIENT: fires hedged attempt A and B (no Idempotency-Key)
EDGE: accepts A on fastpath, then fastpath->slowpath demote at t=2.4s
EDGE: local gateway failover kicks and sends B to upstream as part of failover
UPSTREAM: ACK for A, but TCP reset during trailers; B also delivered -> duplicate
```
Meera Patel: two issues: (1) no common id between hedged attempts and gateway-origin retries, so consumers see two independent deliveries; (2) backpressure window during demotion is small and clients hedge aggressively. we need a lightweight spec to correlate attempts.
Ellen Park: proposal sketch (different from resume-token threads): introduce an "anchor" id that a client can attach when it hedges multiple attempts and the gateway can extend to gateway-origin retries. headers: `Retry-Anchor: <uuid>` and `Retry-Intent: safe|unsafe|idempotent`. semantics: client hedging libraries set Retry-Anchor for all hedged attempts; gateway, when it retries or resumes, copies or maps to that anchor so downstream receivers can treat them as one logical request.
Omar Khan: interesting. anchor solves hedging correlation. need default behavior when client doesn't provide anchor. gateway could synthesize `Retry-Anchor` when it sees hedged attempts by analyzing near-simultaneous connections, but that has risk. better to synthesize only when gateway initiates the retry and include a `X-Edge-Retry-Anchor: <uuid>` to advertise it.
Meera Patel: adds to policy: 1) if client supplies `Retry-Anchor`, gateway uses it for all gateway-origin retries/resumes and includes `X-Edge-Retry-Anchor` when it synthesizes one. 2) `Retry-Intent` is optional but helps downstreams decide whether to dedupe automatically (idempotent = safe to auto-apply). 3) Add `Retry-Decision-Window: <ms>` header from gateway to indicate the short window during which hedges are treated as co-ordinated attempts (default 100ms).
Samir Gupta: operational constraints: we still can't buffer large streaming bodies. Anchor + intent are correlation tools only; they don't enable body replay. Gateway should still reject mid-stream client replays without Idempotency-Key or a resumable token. For streaming routes we keep the 409/425 behavior for safety.
Ellen Park: example header flow when client hedges with anchor:
```
Client attempt A:  Retry-Anchor: 9f8d...  Retry-Intent: unsafe
Client attempt B:  Retry-Anchor: 9f8d...  Retry-Intent: unsafe
Gateway failover -> upstream:  X-Edge-Retry-Anchor: 9f8d...  X-Edge-Retry-Id: <uuid>  X-Edge-Retry-Origin: gateway
```
Omar Khan: add TTL and budgeting: `X-Edge-Retry-TTL: 30` and emit metric `edge.retry.anchor.reused`. also set `Retry-Decision-Window` at ingress so SDKs can tune hedging aggressiveness. if a client hedges outside the Decision-Window, treat as independent requests unless anchor present.
Meera Patel: instrumentation: metrics to add: `edge.retry.anchor.present`, `edge.retry.anchor.synthetic`, `edge.retry.origin.{gateway,client,hedge,upstream}`, `edge.retry.rejected_midstream_no_idempotency`. logs should include both `retry_anchor` and `retry_id` for tracing. billing: requests sharing the same anchor+retry_id should be considered one logical charge when gateway maps them (configurable).
Samir Gupta: example error response when client replays mid-stream without idempotency or token (we keep current safety):
```
HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict
Content-Type: application/json
X-Edge-Retry-Allowed: false

{"error":"retry_requires_idempotency_or_resume","docs":"https://docs.redwood.ai/edge/retries#anchor"}
```
Ellen Park: SDK guidance: 1) hedging libs SHOULD set a strong `Retry-Anchor` UUID for all attempts of the same logical operation. 2) include `Retry-Intent` when client can declare idempotency expectations. 3) SDKs should honor `Retry-Decision-Window` header to avoid overly aggressive hedging. 4) do not auto-retry streaming bodies unless resume token present.
Omar Khan: implement notes: 1) route config opt-in for anchor acceptance; default: on for read-only/idempotent routes, off for non-idempotent unless SDK sets `Retry-Intent=idempotent`. 2) gateway synthesizes `X-Edge-Retry-Anchor` only when it creates a retry and client didn't provide an anchor. 3) GC any synthesized anchor state within TTL and cap anchors-per-tenant to avoid memory blowup.
Meera Patel: test plan: unit tests for header propagation and synthetic-anchor generation, integration test simulating hedged clients within/outside Decision-Window, and a safety test that verifies mid-stream replay rejection still returns 409 and doesn't accept unsafe duplicates. also a load test to validate GC and per-tenant anchor caps.
